Tamoxifen has also been added to regimens, on the hypothesis that melanoma is oestrogen-dependent; an example is the CDBT or Dartmouth regimen (cisplatin, dacarbazine, car- mustine, and tamoxifen). However, a randomised study found that this regimen was no more effective than dacar- bazine alone,19 and there is a lack of evidence that tamoxifen potentiates the action of cytotoxics in melano- ma.17 Although the combination of temozolomide and in- terferon alfa has been reported to increase response rates compared with temozolomide alone, overall survival was no different and toxicity was worse.20 Cytokines such as interferon alfa and interleukin-2 have similar activity to chemotherapy in metastatic melano- ma.17 Cytotoxic chemotherapy has been given with these cytokines and there have been some reports of improved response rates, but large controlled studies are needed to confirm a benefit. Melanoma vaccines are also being used or investigated in metastatic or recurrent disease,15 as are gene therapy, antiangiogenic agents such as thalidomide,17 and the antisense oligonucleotide oblimersen.21 1.
